Interface Mailbox<T>

Type Parameters:
T - the type of value this mailbox delivers
All Known Implementing Classes:
DefaultMailbox
public interface Mailbox<T>
A distributed single-delivery mailbox with TTL-based expiration.

A Mailbox receives exactly one value in its lifetime. Once delivered, the value is observable by any number of subscribers until the mailbox's TTL elapses or delete() is called. After the delivered value has been consumed by a subscriber, the subscription auto-completes. In this sense a mailbox functions as a distributed CompletableFuture — one side creates the mailbox and waits, the other side delivers the single response.

All implementations must be thread-safe. Multiple threads (or distributed nodes) may concurrently attempt to deliver or subscribe without external synchronization.

Usage examples

Blocking pattern: 

// Producer side — elicitation request-response pattern
Mailbox<Response> mailbox =
    mailboxFactory.create("elicit:" + requestId, Response.class, Duration.ofMinutes(5));

// Consumer side — wait for the single delivery (blocking)
BlockingSubscription<Response> sub = mailbox.subscribe();
switch (sub.next(Duration.ofMinutes(5))) {
    case NextResult.Value<Response>(var response) -> handleResponse(response);
    case NextResult.Timeout<Response> t -> handleTimeout();
    case NextResult.Expired<Response> e -> handleExpired();
    case NextResult.Deleted<Response> d -> handleCancelled();
    default -> { }
}

Callback pattern: 

Mailbox<String> mailbox = factory.connect("request-123", String.class);
mailbox.subscribe(value -> System.out.println("Got: " + value));

  • Method Details

    • deliver

      void deliver(T value)
      Deliver a value to this mailbox. A mailbox can receive exactly one delivery in its lifetime — once delivered, the value is observable via subscribe() until the mailbox's TTL elapses or delete() is called.
      Parameters:
      value - the value to deliver
      Throws:
      MailboxExpiredException - if the mailbox has expired or been deleted
      MailboxFullException - if a delivery has already occurred

    • delete

      void delete()
      Delete this mailbox, discarding any undelivered or unconsumed value. Subscribers that are currently waiting will be notified of the deletion. After deletion, subsequent calls to deliver(Object) will throw MailboxExpiredException.

    • subscribe

      BlockingSubscription<T> subscribe()
      Subscribe to the mailbox's single delivery. If the mailbox already has a delivered value when this method is called, the first next() call returns it immediately; otherwise the first next() blocks waiting for delivery. After the single value has been consumed, subsequent next() calls return NextResult.Completed (auto-transition from the underlying SingleShotHandoff).
      Returns:
      a blocking subscription that yields the delivered value and then completes

    • subscribe

      Subscription subscribe(Subscriber<T> subscriber)
      Callback subscribe with a ready-made Subscriber. The subscriber's onNext is invoked exactly once when the single delivery arrives. After the handler returns, the subscription naturally terminates via Completed and the feeder exits.
      Parameters:
      subscriber - the subscriber to deliver the mailbox value to
      Returns:
      a cancellable subscription handle

    • subscribe

      Subscription subscribe(Consumer<SubscriberConfig<T>> customizer)
      Callback subscribe with a SubscriberConfig customizer. onComplete fires after the delivered value is consumed by the handler; onExpiration fires if the mailbox's TTL elapses before delivery; onDelete fires if the mailbox is explicitly deleted before delivery.
      Parameters:
      customizer - lambda that configures the subscriber's handlers
      Returns:
      a cancellable subscription handle

    • key

      String key()
      Returns the unique key that identifies this mailbox within the backing store.
      Returns:
      the mailbox key, never null
